Question 1 (20 marks)
Explain how Crystal Pite communicates personal struggles in Betroffenheit.
In your response, provide specific examples from the work.

items: Components of dance: movement, spatial elements, dynamic elements, dancers, setting and environment; organising the dance through repetition and formal structure.

Dance styles and theatrical elements: contemporary dance, tap dance, cabaret, musical theatre, vaudeville; voice portraying internal voices - alter ego; props, set and staging; music; lighting; costuming.
Repetition, rigid structure, systematic deconstruction and reconstruction.

Personal struggles could include but are not limited to: grief, anger, emptiness, escapism, coping mechanisms, psychological impact, despair, humour, denial, masking pain, finding the thing worth saving which is the memory of those lost.
The work follows the aftermath of the accidental fire that took Crystal Pite's relatives.

Question 2 (10 marks)
Explain how Merce Cunningham extended the boundaries of dance to reflect the era 1955-1975.
In your response, provide specific examples from his works.

items: Cunningham was at the forefront of modern dance for over 50 years due to innovative practices; created Merce Cunningham Dance Company.
Collaborative process relying on the autonomy of music, dance and design; rejected psychological and dramatic content.
Collaborated with renowned musicians, graphic artists and fashion designers to move beyond the world of dance - profound impact on Avant-Garde art.
Manipulated space and time (Points in Space); rejected 'front and centre', encouraging audiences to look at the whole stage; challenged traditional ideas of dance and the role of dancers/audience.
Used the idea of chance and randomness as a creative tool (I Ching, dice, coin toss); dancers were often not informed of the order of sequences until the night of performance.
Rejected storytelling in dance - believed dance did not need a beginning, middle and end; believed the human body was the source of inspiration.
Developed his own dance notation for recording choreography; dancers trained with him formed their own companies continuing his influence.

Question 3 (10 marks)
Explain how Lucinda Childs' ideas about dance have established her as a seminal artist.
In your response, provide specific examples from her works.

items: American postmodern dancer and choreographer; challenged the scope of movement by manipulating movements and complex transitions.
Site-specific works for the first thirteen years of her choreographic journey; took dance to churches, museums, galleries and streets.
Alters the slightest movements into intricate choreography; patterns, repetition and dialect are characteristics unique to her style.
Dance style described as conceptual dance; where dancers are in space, arrangement of sections and order of movements are free.
Beauty lies in spatial exploration and design; uses pedestrian movement such as skipping or turning to create locomotor patterns.
Often pairs movement with monologue (Street Dance 1964); uses music as source of inspiration; musical collaboration with Philip Glass.
Non-traditional audiences eg occupants of a nearby loft; challenged audiences with non-traditional dance; created Lucinda Childs Dance Company.
Worked in opera and ballet as well as her own productions.
